tagline: The FL Players league newsletter · est. 2008
headline: Mikey Finally Wins, and Joey Takes Over Division 1
dek: Inside: Mikey's Monday night comeback, Joey beating Nase while Anthony loses by 54, the division races, a game the kickers decided, the $35 bidding war for Jonah Coleman, and every manager's story.
lead:
Monday night had a hand in five of the six games and flipped one, and it was the one Mikey had been waiting for. Austin led him 112.18 to 96.90 going into Monday. Mikey's players scored 37.38 that night to Austin's 12.0, and Mikey won 134.28 to 124.18 for his first win of the season.

The division race turned on Sunday. Joey beat Nase 126.62 to 105.92 in the game of the week, and Anthony, the model's Division 1 favorite a week ago, lost to Buckley 135.46 to 81.18, the biggest margin of the week. Joey is now 61% to win Division 1 and the bye that comes with it, up from 32%, and Anthony is down to 28% from 55%. In Division 2, James won his fifth straight with a perfect lineup and is 85% to win it.

managers.text: 6-1 and first in points (841.04) after a 123.80 to 79.42 win over Brett without a point left on the bench. Tee Higgins (23.8), Javonte Williams (21.5) and Matthew Stafford (17.5) led it. Then he went shopping: T.J. Hockenson for $7 with Stafford dropped, Makai Lemon for $10, and Caleb Douglas off the free-agent list. His two previous 6-1 starts: a lost final in 2016 and a playoff trip in 2022.
managers.next: Week 8: Buckley, who has won the last four meetings. James leads the series 10-7 and is a 62% favorite.
managers.outlook: The best playoff odds in the league (99%) and the best title odds (31%). Division 2 is his unless something changes fast: the closest team behind him is two games back.

managers.arc: Division 1 leader, and now the favorite
managers.text: Beat Nase 126.62 to 105.92 behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (26.8), Jameson Williams (23.6) and Caleb Williams (22.12), with Bo Nix scoring 26.18 on his bench. Three straight wins, two games up on the rest of Division 1. His two previous 6-1 starts made the playoffs, and the 2022 one won the title.
managers.next: Week 8: Austin, who leads the series 8-6 and has won the last two. Joey is a 55% favorite.
managers.outlook: The model now has him winning the division 61% of the time. He is sixth in points, so the wins have done more than the scoring. Breece Hall was set to be limited in practice Wednesday after missing four straight games, and Braelon Allen is also his.

managers.text: 81.18 against Buckley, the worst loss of the week. Amon-Ra St. Brown (19.7) and D'Andre Swift (17.0) led it, with Chase McLaughlin, a new kicker, at 11.0. Jalen Coker started for 1.4 and KC Concepcion scored 19.2 on the bench. J.J. McCarthy, picked up for Jalen Hurts, started and scored 10.2, and Anthony has since added Kirk Cousins. Still second in points (823.62), and still the team that beats Sleeper's projections by the most, 61.5.
managers.next: Week 8: Nase, a Division 1 game. Anthony has won three straight in the series, leads it 9-4 and is a 65% favorite.
managers.outlook: 87% to make the playoffs, but the division is now Joey's to lose. His two previous 4-3 starts both made the playoffs, and last year's won the title.

managers.text: 88.40 to 87.74 over John, the closest game of the week, and the kickers decided it: Colt's kicker outscored John's 8.0 to 4.0. Rhamondre Stevenson (20.0), Puka Nacua (17.8) and Malik Nabers (14.6) led the lineup, and Tyler Shough scored 13.82 on the bench. He bid $31 on Jonah Coleman and lost by four dollars.
managers.next: Week 8: Mikey, who has won the last two meetings. Colt leads the series 8-6 and is a 57% favorite.
managers.outlook: 66% to make the playoffs, second in Division 2, though two games behind James. His last three weeks average 111.4, the second-hottest hand in the league.

managers.text: 135.46 against Anthony, the high score of the week, with 0.80 left on the bench. Trey McBride (22.1), Luther Burden (21.7) and Christian McCaffrey (19.0) led it. He leads the Coach of the year race at 96% lineup efficiency and has the hottest hand in the league, 112.3 a week over the last three. He also traded with Austin before the week, getting Marvin Harrison Jr. and Jeremiyah Love for Jordyn Tyson, Rico Dowdle and Zach Charbonnet. Lamar Jackson was back on the practice field Wednesday. SKOL.
managers.next: Week 8: James, the game of the week. Buckley has won four straight in the series and is at 38%.
managers.outlook: 63% to make the playoffs. His 4-3 starts are all over the map: seven of them, two lost finals, two other playoff trips and three misses.

managers.text: Lost 126.62 to 105.92 to Joey in the game of the week. Quinshon Judkins (22.9), Jonathan Taylor (18.0) and Emanuel Wilson (18.0) led it; Aaron Rodgers scored 13.08 on the bench and the Broncos defense started for 4.0. Eleventh in points, still 4-3.
managers.next: Week 8: Anthony, a Division 1 game. Anthony has won the last three meetings, and Nase is at 35%.
managers.outlook: 43% to make the playoffs, down from 49%, and 5% to win the division. His three previous 4-3 starts (2014, 2020, 2023) all missed.

managers.text: The quietest score of the week, 76.50, in a loss to T.J. Jahmyr Gibbs (14.8) and Patrick Mahomes (6.0) came in about 13 and 12 under their averages, and Jaylin Noel started for 0.7. One free agent would have flipped it (see the moves). Tyrone Tracy, 8.2 on the bench, went on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. Above the median in five of seven weeks and third in points, but 3-4.
managers.next: Week 8: John. Scott has won six straight in the series, leads it 10-6 and is a 55% favorite.
managers.outlook: 52% to make the playoffs, the scoring keeping him in it. He has never been 3-4 through seven weeks before; his best start was 6-1 in 2023.

managers.text: Beat Scott 87.62 to 76.50 while scoring under the median. CeeDee Lamb (21.9, all on Monday night), Jared Goff (18.02) and Brock Bowers (10.3) did it, and Roschon Johnson started for 1.3. Lamb has 129.0 started points since the preseason trade, and Goff is still the best pickup of the season, 86.8 points in four starts.
managers.next: Week 8: Brett, a rematch of last year's quarterfinal, which T.J. won 111.9 to 90.72. Brett leads the series 15-10, and T.J. is a 54% favorite.
managers.outlook: 37% to make the playoffs and 4% to win Division 1. His three previous 3-4 starts (2016, 2021, 2023) all missed.

managers.text: Lost 123.80 to 79.42 to James with 30.30 left on the bench, the most of the week. Josh Jacobs scored 17.6 there in his first game of the year. C.J. Stroud (16.52), Colston Loveland (16.4) and Jaylen Warren (15.2) led the lineup; Aaron Jones left with a knee injury after 3.1, did not practice Wednesday and is day-to-day. Brett then won the Jonah Coleman bidding (see the moves).
managers.next: Week 8: T.J., a rematch of the quarterfinal Brett lost last year. He is at 46%.
managers.outlook: 26% to make the playoffs. His four previous 3-4 starts: a miss in 2018, playoff trips in 2020 and 2022, and the 2024 title.

managers.text: 87.74 to 88.40 against Colt. Drake Maye (27.44), Ashton Jeanty (17.6) and RJ Harvey (13.0) led it, and Omar Cooper scored 20.0 on the bench. Ted Hurst, a free agent he added, started and scored 0.0, and his kicker scored 4.0 in a game the kickers decided. One free agent would have flipped it too (see the moves). Mike Evans and Brock Purdy are on bye in week 8: two pieces to replace.
managers.next: Week 8: Scott, who has won six straight in the series. John is at 45%.
managers.outlook: 18% to make the playoffs. His five previous 2-5 starts all missed.

managers.text: Scored 124.18, well above the median, and lost after leading Mikey by 15.28 going into Monday night. Joe Burrow scored 28.88 in his first start for Austin, with Bucky Irving (23.5) and Tre Tucker (18.8) behind him. The Jets defense started for 1.0. He traded with Buckley before the week, and Rico Dowdle, one of the backs he got, scored 11.6 on his bench.
managers.next: Week 8: Joey. Austin has won the last two meetings and is at 45%.
managers.outlook: 12% to make the playoffs and a 20% chance at last place. His two previous 2-5 starts, in 2008 and 2014, missed.

tags.t: Most points left on the bench

managers.text: The first win, 134.28 to 124.18 over Austin, the second-best score of the week. Tony Pollard scored 35.0, the best player of the week, with Zay Flowers (23.7) and Dak Prescott (23.28) behind him. Nico Collins started for 1.6, and Cam Skattebo scored 18.6 on the bench. Saquon Barkley came back on Monday night, then tweaked the hamstring and picked up a back issue. Jordan Mason is back from injured reserve.
managers.next: Week 8: Colt. Mikey has won the last two meetings and is at 43%.
managers.outlook: 3% to make the playoffs: none of the 12 teams in league history to start 1-6 got in. He is 48% to finish last, which is not board duty: that goes to the loser of the losers bracket. Collins is on bye in week 8, and so is his kicker, Ka'imi Fairbairn: two pieces to replace.

trends.title: What seven weeks means here
trends.text: Both 7-0 teams in league history made the playoffs. 6-1 teams made it 8 times in 9, 5-2 teams 85% of the time, 4-3 teams 61%, 3-4 teams 43% and 2-5 teams 13%.

trends.title: Scoring
trends.text: Week 7 averaged 104.3 a team, up from 94.0, the season low, the week before.

trends.title: The kicker file
trends.text: Colt over John is the second game this season the kickers decided: take both out and John wins. The first was Joey over John in week 2. John has been on the wrong end of both.

history.title: Week 7, all time
history.text: The highest week 7 score on record is T.J.'s 168.64 against Mikey in 2018. The biggest week 7 blowout was Quool over The Guru's, 125 to 50, in 2010. The closest was Joey over Mikey, 98.22 to 98.1, in 2022.

ahead: Game of the week: James and Buckley in Division 2. James is 6-1, but Buckley has won the last four meetings. Also worth watching: Anthony and Nase in Division 1, where Anthony needs the win to stay close to Joey, and T.J. against Brett in a rematch of last year's quarterfinal.

moves.intro: One trade, a $35 bidding war, and three games the waiver wire would have flipped.

items.title: Buckley and Austin
items.text: Buckley got Marvin Harrison Jr. and Jeremiyah Love. Austin got Jordyn Tyson, Rico Dowdle and Zach Charbonnet.
items.verdict: Austin's second trade in two weeks. Neither side started a piece of it in week 7.

items.title: Six bids for Jonah Coleman
items.text: Brett won the Denver running back for $35, dropping C.J. Stroud, the quarterback he had claimed for $13 before week 7. Colt bid $31, James $30, Austin $27, Scott $22 and Buckley $6.
items.verdict: Six bids, the most for any player this week.

items.title: Three flips from the wire
items.text: Mason Taylor scored 22.7 while unrostered that week; in for Jaylin Noel, he flips Scott's 11.12 loss to T.J. The Tampa Bay defense scored 24.0 unrostered; in for the Jets defense, it flips Austin's 10.10 loss to Mikey. Caleb Douglas scored 20.0 unrostered; in for Ted Hurst, he flips John's 0.66 loss to Colt.

items.title: The Allen trade, two weeks in
items.text: Burrow's first start for Austin was 28.88. Irving has 29.4 in two starts and Juwan Johnson 0.0 in one. Allen has one start for James, 18.3, and was on bye in week 7.
items.verdict: James is 2-0 since the trade, Austin 0-2.

nfl.note: Headlines as ESPN reported them on the date shown. Injury and depth-chart news can change before kickoff.
nfl.intro: Scott loses Tyrone Tracy to injured reserve, Brett has Aaron Jones day-to-day and Josh Jacobs back, and Mikey's Saquon Barkley came out of his return banged up.

items.headline: Packers activate RB Josh Jacobs for 2026 debut
items.note: Brett's Jacobs had 11 carries for 36 yards and a receiving touchdown, on Brett's bench.

items.headline: Giants place RB Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR with hamstring injury
items.note: Scott's Tracy is on injured reserve. Mikey has Cam Skattebo, and the Giants are on bye this week.

items.headline: Vikings RB Jones avoids serious knee injury, day-to-day
items.note: Brett's Jones did not practice Wednesday. Mikey has Jordan Mason, who out-carried Jones on Sunday.

items.headline: Eagles' Saquon Barkley says hamstring 'great' in return, not sweating back issue
items.note: Mikey's Barkley had 62 yards and a touchdown on seven carries.

items.headline: Ravens' Jesse Minter optimistic QB Lamar Jackson can return vs. Bills
items.note: Buckley has Jackson. Colt has Derrick Henry and Mikey has Zay Flowers in that offense.

items.headline: Vikings activate RB Jordan Mason off injured reserve
items.note: Mikey's Mason ran 15 times for 68 yards in his first game back.

items.headline: Bo Nix wows with 62-yard run as Broncos stand by 'our guy' at QB after win
items.note: Joey has Nix. Brett now has Jonah Coleman in that backfield, and John has RJ Harvey.

items.headline: Why Derrick Henry has taken Jets RB Braelon Allen under his wing
items.note: Joey has Allen and Breece Hall, Colt has Henry.

features.label: The races
features.title: Two divisions, two byes
features.dek: The byes go to the division winners, not the two best records.

blocks.text: A week ago Division 1 had a leader and a different favorite. Now they are the same team. Joey is two games up on everyone, and the one team the model still gives a real chance, Anthony, outscores him by about 13 points a week and plays Nase next.

James is two games clear with seven to play and the most points in the league. The way back in for anyone else starts this week: he plays Buckley, the one team in the division that has had his number lately.
Chances come from 10,000 simulated finishes of the season after week 7. A tie for a division is broken on points in the model.
Byes: Houston, New Orleans, the Giants and San Francisco
John loses Mike Evans and Brock Purdy, and Mikey loses Nico Collins and his kicker. Scott's Tyrone Tracy and Mikey's Cam Skattebo are Giants, so neither plays.

items: Brett: Aaron Jones did not practice Wednesday and is day-to-day with a knee injury.
Scott: Tyrone Tracy is on injured reserve.
Joey: Breece Hall was set to be limited in Wednesday's practice.
Mikey: Saquon Barkley tweaked his hamstring and has a new back issue from Monday night.
Buckley: Lamar Jackson was on the practice field Wednesday.
